title: A quotient of a G-ring is a G-ring
statement: Let $R$ be a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal. Then the quotient ring $R/I$ is a G-ring. (Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PP, item (3), applied to the surjection $R\to R/I$, which is of finite type and quasi-finite.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite, line 12214), item (3): 'If R -> R' is quasi-finite and R is a G-ring, then R' is a G-ring', applied to R' = R/I; this is how the proof of Proposition 07PV (line 12558) uses it ('Writing S as a quotient of R[x_1,...,x_n] we see from Lemma 07PP that it suffices to prove that R[x_1,...,x_n] is a G-ring').

proof.text: Let $q:R\to S=R/I$ be the quotient map. Since $R$ is a G-ring it is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], and $S$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra ($S\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/\mathfrak a$ with $n=0$, $\mathfrak a=I$), so $S$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. By the definition of a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] it remains to show: for every prime ideal $\bar{\mathfrak p}\subset S$ the completion map $c_S:S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}\to(S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge$ at the maximal ideal $\bar{\mathfrak p}S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ is regular. Fix $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ and put $\mathfrak p=q^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak p})$, a prime ideal of $R$ containing $I=\ker q$; as $q$ is surjective, $q(\mathfrak p)=\bar{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite, line 12214), proof (lines 12236-12257), for R' = R/I

proof.text: Put $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$ and $J=IA$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] (applied to the identity of the Noetherian ring $R$ at $\mathfrak p$) $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is a Noetherian local ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] the map $\lambda:A\to S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$, $r/s\mapsto q(r)/q(s)$, is a surjective ring map with kernel $J$. Its image of $\mathfrak m$ is the maximal ideal: for $a\in\mathfrak p$, $\lambda(a/s)=q(a)/q(s)\in\bar{\mathfrak p}S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$; conversely $\lambda(\mathfrak m)$ is an ideal of $S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ ($\lambda$ is surjective) containing the generators $q(a)/1=\lambda(a/1)$, $a\in\mathfrak p$, of $\bar{\mathfrak p}S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ (recall $\bar{\mathfrak p}=q(\mathfrak p)$) [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. So $\lambda(\mathfrak m)=\bar{\mathfrak p}S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$, and $(S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge$ is the $\lambda(\mathfrak m)$-adic completion of $S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient, line 1380), with S = R \ p

proof.text: Since $R$ is a G-ring and $\mathfrak p$ is prime, the completion map $c_A:A\to A^\wedge=\varprojlim_nA/\mathfrak m^n$ is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. The ring map $\lambda:A\to S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ is surjective, hence of finite type ($S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ is generated by $1$ as an $A$-algebra). By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change] applied to $\varphi=c_A$ and $A\to S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$, the base change $\beta:S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}\to A^\wedge\otimes_AS_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$, $y\mapsto1\otimes y$, is regular. (This is the step 'R'_{p'} -> (R'_{p'})^ is a base change of R_p -> R_p^' of the proof of 07PP; the fibre argument given there is the proof of 07C1.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite, line 12214), proof (lines 12236-12257), for R' = R/I

proof.text: Identify the target of $\beta$ with $(S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge$. Via the isomorphism $A/J\cong S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ induced by $\lambda$ (Step 2), [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] applied to $c_A:A\to A^\wedge$ and the ideal $J$ gives a ring isomorphism $\alpha:A^\wedge\otimes_AS_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}\xrightarrow{\sim}A^\wedge/JA^\wedge$, $x\otimes\lambda(a)\mapsto x\,c_A(a)\bmod JA^\wedge$; thus $\alpha(\beta(\lambda(a)))=c_A(a)\bmod JA^\wedge$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] applied to the Noetherian local ring $(A,\mathfrak m)$ and the surjection $\lambda$ with kernel $J$ and $\lambda(\mathfrak m)=\bar{\mathfrak p}S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ (Step 2), the induced map $\theta:A^\wedge\to(S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is surjective with kernel $JA^\wedge$ and $\theta\circ c_A=c_S\circ\lambda$, so it induces a ring isomorphism $\bar\theta:A^\wedge/JA^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}(S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge$ with $\bar\theta(c_A(a)\bmod JA^\wedge)=c_S(\lambda(a))$. Hence $\Phi=\bar\theta\circ\alpha:A^\wedge\otimes_AS_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}\to(S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge$ is a ring isomorphism with $\Phi\circ\beta=c_S$ (both send $\lambda(a)$ to $c_S(\lambda(a))$, and $\lambda$ is surjective). (In the proof of 07PP this is $R_{\mathfrak p}^\wedge\otimes_RR'=(R'_{\mathfrak p'})^\wedge\times B$ of Algebra 07NC, here with $B=0$.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite, line 12214), proof (lines 12236-12257), for R' = R/I

proof.text: Regularity is invariant under isomorphism of algebras: since $\Phi$ is an isomorphism of $S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$-algebras from $\beta$ to $c_S$ (Step 4), $(S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge$ is flat over $S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ because $A^\wedge\otimes_AS_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ is, and for every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$, $\Phi\otimes\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is an isomorphism of $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$-algebras between the fibre rings, so the fibre rings of $c_S$ are Noetherian and geometrically regular because those of $\beta$ are (Step 3) [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Thus $c_S$ is regular; as $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ was arbitrary and $S$ is Noetherian (Step 1), $S=R/I$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

split_report.summary: Read Stacks 07PP and its proof (via Algebra 07NC and base change of geometric regularity). Instead of stating 07PP(3) for all quasi-finite maps (which would need 07NC, i.e. Zariski's main theorem through lemma-quasi-finite-open-integral-closure, unnecessary here), wrote the 07PP proof specialized to R -> R/I, where 07NC holds with B = 0: for a prime p/I, (R/I)_{p/I} = R_p/IR_p (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient, Stacks 00CT), the completion of R_p/IR_p is R_p^/IR_p^ = R_p^ (x) R_p/IR_p (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient, Stacks 00MA, with lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change), so its completion map is the base change of the regular map R_p -> R_p^ along the finite type map R_p -> R_p/IR_p, regular by lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change (07C1). Statement and stmt_deps unchanged. Tags verified in tags/tags: 07PP, 07C1, 07BZ, 07NC, 00MA, 00CT; 07PN is lemma-check-G-ring-easy (not used). Mathlib has no G-ring theory (searches recorded at creation).

reviewed.note: Reviewed by the lead (opus-relaunch6). Direct argument for a quotient (the 07PP proof specialised to R -> R/I; the general 07PP(3) would need 07NC and Zariski's main theorem): R/I Noetherian, R_p -> (R/I)_{p-bar} surjective with kernel IR_p (new Mathlib leaf of three declarations: the IsLocalization instance for quotients Localization/Ideal.lean:391, Ideal.map_primeCompl_comap_of_surjective Ideal/Maps.lean:514, IsLocalization.algEquiv Localization/Basic.lean:172; lines verified), regularity of R_p -> R_p^ base changed along the finite type map (07C1 node), R_p^ (x) (R/I)_{p-bar} = R_p^/IR_p^ = ((R/I)_{p-bar})^ (tensor-quotient leaf and new unsplit node for 00MA(2),(3): completion of a quotient of a Noetherian local ring), regularity invariant under isomorphism (elementary). Brief errors: 07PN is check-G-ring-easy, 07BZ the definition of regular, 0315 completion-generalities; 00MA is the completion-of-quotient lemma. Possible duplicate to check at the review of complete-local-g-ring: a completion-of-quotient node.
